revisionNotes: Revision 2 (D-084 r2): size limits for the definition, the semantic.propose transport and the bundle; code trimming per ouf.value-types.v1 'whitespace'; optional proposal rationale with the source column; review projection rendered by the THS that already renders semantic approvals; distinct column values for the agent. Revision 1 had SHA-256 2f4528eb4c9c6bd9d2c6345464c8292f0cb3f36834cb2f54f81ae20e3dbe4a71.
extends: ouf.value-types.v1 revision 2 (sha256 3b85052e253b985f1082527eb595d2f02e5336047203deb3503a9766c1324295); this document defines the published value map that VALUE_MAP_V1 and conceptMembership (b) refer to.
principle: A value map is a governed, immutable Semantic Registry artifact of type VALUE_MAP. It maps the source codes of a column to CONCEPT artifacts of one target VOCABULARY. The agent proposes it through MCP capabilities, typically from the distinct values of a profiled column; a human approves it on the THS; it is published in a publication set and pinned by mappings as <semanticId>@<publicationSetId>, exactly like a DATATYPE.

artifact.owner: Semantic Registry (new artifact_type VALUE_MAP, additive migration, D-080: the predecessor keeps working on a database that contains VALUE_MAP rows)
artifact.lifecycle: Same as DATATYPE: native proposal through MCP semantic.propose, THS approval, publication in a publication set, lifecycle ACTIVE -> DEPRECATED -> RETIRED. Immutable once published: a change is a new semanticVersion.

definition.targetVocabulary: Required. '<VOCABULARY semanticId>@<publicationSetId>' of a PUBLISHED, ACTIVE vocabulary at proposal time.
definition.entries: Required. 1 to 2000 items {code, concept}, in any order; the registry stores and returns them sorted by code (String.compareTo, i.e. UTF-16 code unit order).
definition.code: String, compared exactly after the VALUE_MAP_V1 trim (whitespace as defined in ouf.value-types.v1 'whitespace'): 1 to 128 characters (Unicode code points), no leading or trailing whitespace, no control characters (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F). Unique within the map (exact, case sensitive).
definition.concept: semanticId of a CONCEPT that is a member of targetVocabulary in the publication set of the targetVocabulary pin. Several codes may map to the same concept. At most 512 characters.
definition.labels: Optional {it, en} display labels of the map, like other artifacts.
definition.closed: No other keys are allowed in the definition or in an entry.

artifact.digest: definitionSha256 = SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the definition (UTF-8, object keys sorted, no insignificant whitespace, entries sorted by code), computed by the registry exactly like the DATATYPE definitionSha256.
artifact.resolve: GET /api/semantic/v1/references:resolve?semanticId=<id>&publicationSetId=<set> returns, for a VALUE_MAP, the same envelope as for a DATATYPE: artifact_type 'VALUE_MAP', status (ACTIVE | DEPRECATED | RETIRED), revision_id, publication_set_id, definition (canonical, entries sorted) and definitionSha256.
artifact.validation: The registry rejects a proposal whose targetVocabulary is not a published vocabulary, whose concepts are not members of it, or that breaks the limits above, with SEMANTIC_VALUE_MAP_INVALID and no source values in the message (D-058).

limits.definitionBytes: The canonical JSON of the definition is at most 786432 bytes (UTF-8). Semantic Registry and MCP reject a larger definition (SEMANTIC_VALUE_MAP_INVALID, INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS).
limits.transport: semantic.propose with artifactType VALUE_MAP accepts arguments up to 1048576 bytes end to end: MCP argument bound, Gateway route schema and body limit, Semantic Registry receipt/delegation verification. Other artifact types keep their current bounds. Proof: a signed envelope with 2000 entries of maximum length crosses MCP, Gateway and the owner.
limits.bundle: The canonical JSON of all value map definitions embedded in one bundle totals at most 1048576 bytes. Onboarding rejects the preparation with ONB_VALUE_MAP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; Ingestion rejects a larger bundle with ING_VALUE_MAP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Ingestion accepts a frozen configuration response of up to 3145728 bytes.

artifact.proposalRationale: semantic.propose may carry, outside the definition and outside the digest, rationale {sourceColumn: {fieldName (1 to 256 characters), sourceId?}} naming the profiled column the agent used. The registry stores it with the proposal and projects it in the review; it never contains source values.

pinning.onboarding: Onboarding resolves every valueMapRef used by a field, a constructor input or a LIST_SPLIT_V1 itemReaderParams through references:resolve. New preparations require status ACTIVE. Onboarding embeds in the published bundle, for every pinned value map: {valueMapRef: '<semanticId>@<publicationSetId>', revisionId, targetVocabulary, definition, definitionSha256}. Historical rereads serve the frozen bundle without querying the current status.
pinning.ingestion: Ingestion verifies the embedded definition and definitionSha256 against references:resolve (same port and rules as DATATYPE: ACTIVE for readiness, ACTIVE | DEPRECATED | RETIRED for an already published bundle), then applies VALUE_MAP_V1 with the embedded entries. An unmapped code is ING_TRANSFORM_VALUE_INVALID with rowOrdinal and without the value. A pin without embedded definition stays ING_VALUE_MAP_CONTENT_REQUIRED.
pinning.udp: Unchanged: membership (b) uses the embedded pin and targetVocabulary; UDP does not need the entries.

ths: Semantic Registry projects on the semantic approval card a valueMapReview object: {name, targetVocabulary {label, semanticId, publicationSetId}, entryCount, entries [{code, concept, conceptLabel}] sorted by code, sourceColumn?, changes? {added [code], removed [code], changed [{code, from, to}]} against the previous semanticVersion}. The THS page that already renders semantic approvals (Onboarding workflow-review, flow 'semantic', the same place as datatypeReview) renders it in Italian: name, target vocabulary (label and identifier), the code -> concept table with concept labels (paginated or scrollable, readable at 375 px), the number of entries, the source column when present and the differences. The Semantic Registry ships the projection, not a separate UI component.
mcp: semantic.propose accepts artifactType VALUE_MAP with the definition above (argument schema closed, limits enforced before forwarding). The agent builds the entries from distinctValues of a profiled column (source_file_profile) and from the concepts of a published vocabulary (semantic_search / semantic_get); it never invents concepts. The tool descriptions explain when to propose a value map: a column of codes whose values belong to a controlled vocabulary.
gateway: The semantic.propose route schema accepts the VALUE_MAP definition with the same closed shape and limits.
profile: Onboarding source_file_profile returns, for each column whose trimmed non-empty values have at most 2000 distinct values of at most 128 characters each, the sorted list distinctValues (exact trimmed values) under the same authorization, data access labels and redaction rules as source_file_preview; for any other column distinctValues is absent and only the counts are returned. MCP passes distinctValues through unchanged and the agent builds value map entries from it.
